div.head: Ger 3
div.ab: Gyf he wel aginnan wile ne mæig he sleac beon ne to ofer hydig ac he mot ægðer witan ge læsse ge mare ge betere ge mætre ðæs ðe to tune belimpð . ge on tune . ge on dune . ge on wuda . ge on wæ|tere. ge on felda. ge on falda . ge inne . ge ute.

If he wants to perform well, he must not be slack nor over-cautious, but he must know both the lesser and the greater, both the better and the poorer of that which pertains to the estate, both in the farmyard and on the hills, both in the woodlands and on the waters, both in the fields and the folds, both indoors and outdoors.

[3] Gyf he wel aginnan wile, ne mæig he sleac beon ne to oferhydig; ac he mot æðger witan ge læsse ge mare, ge betere ge mætre ðæs ðe to tune belimpð, ge on tune ge on dune, ge on wuda ge on wætere, ge on felda ge on falde, ge inne ge ute.
